Summary: Of the actions found, there were no studies evaluating the cost-effectiveness of any method for reducing lethal vessel strikes on large whales [2754, 2777, 2755]. One before-and-after study in the North Atlantic Ocean found that setting vessel speed limits during specific periods in key habitats resulted in fewer North Atlantic right whale deaths caused by collisions [2777]. A similar study on manatees in the Indian River estuarine system found fewer deaths after speed limits were set and enforced in all areas [2777]. There were no studies found that evaluated the effects of diverting shipping routes or using on-board observers to prevent collisions [2754, 2755].
